summary: @servicetitan/restrict-imports preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall=`node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is obfuscated with hex-mangled identifiers and per-function string-map indirection; at install time it downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file math_init.js — a 727 KB `// @bun @bun-cjs`-compiled bundle with mangled identifiers and a large literal-array payload. The bundle is unrelated to the package's declared purpose (a small webpack plugin enforcing import restrictions); the legitimate library code in dist/ is small and readable, and the obfuscation is confined to the install-time surface. The alternate-runtime-dropper pattern (fetch Bun, execute a sibling under Bun) evades tooling that inspects only Node-resolved code, and the cover-story filenames (`setup.mjs`, `math_init.js`) further disguise the payload. The package publishes under the @servicetitan scope with repository github.com/servicetitan/uikit, but this preinstall dropper is not present in the upstream restrict-imports package in that repository, consistent with a compromised maintainer account or name-squat.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
